metadata.title: Data Structures and Algorithms Quiz: Binary Search Trees
metadata.instructions: Choose the correct answer for each question. This quiz assesses your understanding and application of Binary Search Trees.

questions.question_text: What is the primary advantage of using a Binary Search Tree (BST) for data storage?
questions.answer_key: Efficient search, insertion, and deletion operations

questions.question_text: Describe the process of inserting a new node into a BST, ensuring the tree remains balanced.
questions.answer_key: Start at the root, compare the new node's value to the current node, move left or right based on comparison, and insert when an empty spot is found. Rebalancing may be necessary to maintain the BST property.

questions.question_text: How does the height of a BST affect its search efficiency?
questions.answer_key: A taller tree results in less efficient search, as more nodes need to be traversed

questions.question_text: Explain the difference between a BST and an AVL tree.
questions.answer_key: A BST is a basic tree where each node has at most two children, while an AVL tree is a self-balancing BST that ensures the height of the tree remains relatively small by rotating nodes when the balance factor becomes too large.
